s: A data processing application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Each month the instances read and write about 400 TB of data in Amazon S3 buckets in the same Region. All traffic to Amazon S3 currently goes through a NAT gateway, and NAT gateway data processing charges are now a large part of the bill. The instances must not have public IP addresses. Which solution is the MOST cost-effective?
o: Create an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC and associate it with the route tables of the private subnets.
Create an S3 interface endpoint in each Availability Zone and update the application to use the endpoint-specific DNS names.
Move the instances to public subnets and assign Elastic IP addresses so that traffic to Amazon S3 bypasses the NAT gateway.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the buckets and update the application to use the accelerated endpoint.

w.y: A gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 adds a route (prefix list) to the subnet route tables, so S3 traffic leaves the VPC without passing through the NAT gateway. Gateway endpoints have no hourly or per-GB charge. Their limit: they work only for traffic from inside the VPC in the same Region, not from on-premises or other Regions, which is when interface endpoints are needed.

o.A: Correct. Removes the NAT processing charge for S3 traffic at no extra cost.
o.B: Interface endpoints also avoid the NAT gateway but charge per hour per AZ plus per GB processed. At 400 TB a month that is far more than a free gateway endpoint.
o.D: Transfer Acceleration speeds up long-distance uploads over the internet for an extra fee. It does not help same-Region traffic and adds cost.
